blocks.en:
Diagnostics: The first surgical action is review of the Table 1 hormonal
and tumor-marker results (hCG, LH, FSH, estradiol, testosterone,
prolactin, thyroid function, DHEA-S, 17-OHP, androstenedione as
available) and of the chest imaging performed 13 days after the
endocrinology visit. The expected result is normal age-appropriate
gonadotropin/steroid profile and a chest image without intrathoracic or
osseous lesion; this would reinforce the idiopathic/localized diagnosis
and permit a targeted surgical plan. If any hormonal value is abnormal
(for example elevated hCG, elevated estradiol, or suppressed LH/FSH),
the surgical plan must be deferred in favor of endocrine and oncologic
work-up, because the breast mass may then be a manifestation of a
gonadal or extragonadal tumor and not an isolated surgical problem. The
second action is a focused surgical examination under anesthesia at the
time of planned excision to confirm that the mass is indeed discrete,
mobile, retroareolar, and not fixed to pectoralis fascia or skin, and to
inspect for any clinically occult contralateral lesion. The third action
is complete excisional biopsy of the right retroareolar mass through a
periareolar or circumareolar incision, with the specimen sent for
histopathology in fresh, oriented, and inked form. The expected result
is definitive histologic diagnosis distinguishing usual ductal
hyperplasia from a fibroepithelial or other neoplasm, and this result
will determine all subsequent management. If histology returns as usual
ductal hyperplasia/stromal fibrosis consistent with gynecomastia, no
further surgical treatment is needed and the family is counseled that
recurrence on the contralateral side is possible during puberty. If
histology returns as a fibroepithelial neoplasm (for example juvenile
fibroadenoma), complete excision is considered adequate therapy provided
margins are uninvolved; the contralateral left 'breast
bud' is observed. If histology is malignant, the
patient is referred immediately to pediatric oncology for staging (chest
imaging, breast MRI if indicated, axillary ultrasound, and systemic
work-up) and for multidisciplinary surgical-oncologic planning.
Treatment: The principal treatment proposed at this preconcilium stage
is right periareolar excisional biopsy of the retroareolar mass as a
combined diagnostic and therapeutic maneuver, performed under general
anesthesia, with the patient supine, the arm on the side of the lesion
abducted, and a small inferior or lateral periareolar incision planned
to preserve nipple-areolar viability and to allow access to the
retroareolar disc. The rationale is that the lesion is unilateral,
persistent for 18 months, enlarging, >2 cm clinically, and
sonographically solid, and therefore exceeds the threshold for simple
observation of prepubertal gynecomastia. The goal of the operation is
complete excision of the mass with a small margin of surrounding breast
tissue, hemostasis, and preservation of the nipple-areolar complex;
criteria for surgical readiness are normal coagulation, normal
preoperative endocrine panel (or endocrinology clearance if any value is
abnormal), and signed informed consent including discussion of risks of
hematoma, seroma, infection, nipple-areolar compromise, scarring,
recurrence, and the possibility of finding an unexpected neoplasm.
Pharmacologic treatment is not indicated preoperatively; the topical
triamcinolone for eczema should be continued and is not a
contraindication. Postoperative care includes a soft dressing,
analgesia, activity restriction for 1–2 weeks, and wound review at 1–2
weeks with pathology results; no hormonal therapy is initiated.
Effectiveness and safety monitoring is by histopathology of the excised
specimen (definitive diagnostic endpoint) and by clinical wound review
at 1–2 weeks and again at 3 months to detect recurrence, contour
deformity, or contralateral changes. Expectations from adjacent
specialties: endocrinology is asked to provide the numeric Table 1
results and interpretation, and to confirm that no treatable endocrine
cause is present before the surgical date; radiology is asked to make
the breast ultrasound images available intraoperatively and to comment
on the chest imaging already performed; pathology is asked to process
the specimen for routine histology and to retain tissue for potential
additional stains if a fibroepithelial or unusual lesion is identified;
oncology is on standby in the unlikely event of malignancy.

blocks.en:
This 8-year-old, phenotypically normal boy with a unilateral, firm,
mobile, 2 × \times 2 cm, non-adherent, enlarging right retroareolar mass
present for 18 months, accompanied by only minimal contralateral breast
tissue and very early pubic/axillary hair, prepubertal testicular volume
of 3 ml, prepubertal phallus, bone age equal to chronologic age (8
years), and a sonographically well-circumscribed, oval, hypoechoic,
hypovascular retroareolar lesion without features of malignancy,
presents as a surgical case at the preconcilium stage with a working
diagnosis of persistent idiopathic prepubertal unilateral gynecomastia
or a benign fibroepithelial lesion (high probability), with
juvenile-type fibroepithelial neoplasm as an intermediate alternative
and prepubertal male breast malignancy as a low-probability but
mandatory-to-exclude category (DOI: 10.1056/NEJMcpc1503831 ). The first
surgical priority is to obtain and review the Table 1 hormonal and
tumor-marker results and the chest imaging already performed before the
operative date, because any abnormal endocrine value would redirect
management away from a straightforward excisional biopsy and toward an
endocrine or oncologic work-up. Once the endocrine panel is confirmed
normal, the priority surgical action is right periareolar excisional
biopsy of the retroareolar mass for definitive histologic diagnosis,
which simultaneously serves as treatment if the lesion proves to be a
benign fibroepithelial tumor, while malignancy—though unlikely on the
available imaging—must be definitively excluded by tissue. The data
gaps with the greatest impact on the surgical decision are the missing
numeric values from Table 1 (hCG, LH, FSH, estradiol, testosterone,
prolactin, adrenal steroids) and the formal report of the chest imaging
study, both of which must be reviewed before the patient is taken to the
operating room. With those data available and reviewed, the proposed
preconcilium plan is a single, definitive excisional biopsy via a
periareolar approach, with endocrinology providing preoperative
clearance, radiology providing intraoperative ultrasound support,
pathology providing definitive histology, and pediatric oncology on
standby only if malignancy is unexpectedly identified (DOI: 10.1056/NEJMcpc1503831 ).

blocks.en:
Approximately 18 months before presentation (2014-2015), the parents
noted a mass under the right nipple without discharge (DOI: 10.1056/NEJMcpc1503831 ). This establishes chronicity and benign initial
behavior. Six months before presentation, the mass enlarged and fine
pubic hair was noted (DOI: 10.1056/NEJMcpc1503831 ), suggesting hormonal
stimulation coinciding with adrenarche. At presentation (2016), physical
exam revealed a firm, mobile 2x2 cm mass under the right areola not
adherent to skin, a small amount of soft left breast tissue, fine pubic
and scant axillary hair, and prepubertal testes (3 ml) with a
prepubertal phallus (DOI: 10.1056/NEJMcpc1503831 ). This indicates a
unilateral discrete mass with early sexual hair but prepubertal gonads.
A radiograph of the left hand showed a bone age of 8 years, consistent
with chronological age (DOI: 10.1056/NEJMcpc1503831 ), excluding advanced
skeletal maturation. Eight days after the visit, laboratory tests were
performed (Table 1), but the values are not provided in the available
text (DOI: 10.1056/NEJMcpc1503831 ), creating a critical data gap
regarding hormone levels. Thirteen days after the visit, imaging studies
of the chest were performed, but the modality and findings are not
provided (DOI: 10.1056/NEJMcpc1503831 ), creating another explicit data
gap. Breast ultrasound (Figure 1) revealed a well-circumscribed, oval,
hypoechoic, mobile mass (1.4x1.3x0.8 cm) in the retroareolar region with
smooth margins, through-transmission, parallel orientation, and minimal
peripheral flow, without spiculation, calcifications, or increased
vascularity; the left breast showed a normal bud (DOI: 10.1056/NEJMcpc1503831 ). These features are characteristic of a benign
solid lesion.

blocks.en:
The dominant imaging-supported syndrome is a unilateral,
benign-appearing retroareolar breast mass. This is confirmed by the
sonographic findings of a well-circumscribed, oval, hypoechoic, mobile
mass with smooth margins, through-transmission, parallel orientation,
and minimal peripheral flow (DOI: 10.1056/NEJMcpc1503831 , Figure 1). The
mechanism involves hormone-sensitive proliferation of breast tissue;
however, the discrete, nodular morphology suggests a localized
fibroepithelial proliferation (such as a fibroadenoma) rather than the
diffuse ductal and stromal proliferation typical of gynecomastia. A
second relevant syndrome is early adrenarche, supported by the presence
of fine, straight, lightly pigmented pubic hairs and scant axillary
hairs at age 8, alongside prepubertal testes (3 mL) and a prepubertal
phallus (DOI: 10.1056/NEJMcpc1503831 ). This is realized through early
adrenal androgen production, which can be peripherally aromatized to
estrogen, potentially stimulating localized breast tissue growth. The
concordance of bone age with chronologic age (8 years) argues against a
long-standing, advanced systemic sex-steroid effect. Considered but
rejected is true central precocious puberty, as the testes remain
prepubertal in volume and the bone age is not advanced.

blocks.en:
High probability: Juvenile fibroadenoma. Arguments for: the mass is
discrete, oval, well-circumscribed, and hypoechoic with
through-transmission and smooth margins—classic features of a
fibroadenoma; fibroadenomas can occur in males during periods of
hormonal change. Arguments against: rare in prepubertal males. What
would confirm: histology showing biphasic proliferation of stroma and
epithelium. What would refute: regression or evolution into fan-shaped
tissue on follow-up. Medium probability: Unilateral gynecomastia.
Arguments for: retroareolar location, recent enlargement, and background
of early adrenarche with possible estrogen effect. Arguments against:
gynecomastia typically appears as fan-shaped, hypoechoic tissue blending
with surrounding fat, not a discrete, mobile mass with a capsule-like
margin. What would confirm: resolution or flattening on follow-up
without intervention. What would refute: persistence as a discrete
nodule. Medium probability: Gynecomastia secondary to an estrogen- or
hCG-secreting testicular or adrenal tumor. Arguments for: unilateral
breast enlargement and early pubic hair in a prepubertal boy. Arguments
against: no palpable testicular mass, bone age is not advanced. What
would confirm: scrotal or adrenal imaging demonstrating a mass, or
elevated estradiol/hCG on laboratory testing. What would refute: normal
testicular and adrenal imaging. Low probability but must be excluded:
Male breast carcinoma. Arguments for: any solid breast mass warrants
consideration of malignancy; remote family history of breast cancer.
Arguments against: benign sonographic features lacking irregular
margins, calcifications, and hypervascularity; exceedingly rare in
prepubertal children. What would confirm: aggressive sonographic
features or biopsy. What would refute: benign histology or long-term
stability.

blocks.en:
Diagnostics: The primary goal is to confirm the benign nature of the
mass and exclude rare pathologic hormone sources. Scrotal ultrasound
with color Doppler is the next essential imaging step to exclude a
small, non-palpable estrogen-secreting testicular tumor (e.g., Leydig
cell tumor). If scrotal ultrasound is normal, adrenal imaging (MRI or
contrast-enhanced CT) should be considered if pending laboratory values
(Table 1) suggest an adrenal source of estrogen excess. Follow-up breast
ultrasound in 3 to 6 months is recommended to document interval
stability; development of irregular margins, increased vascularity, or
calcifications would prompt ultrasound-guided core biopsy. Treatment:
Conservative observation is the appropriate initial approach given the
benign imaging phenotype. Pharmacologic therapy or surgical excision is
not indicated unless the mass grows disproportionately, becomes
symptomatic, or develops suspicious imaging features. Expectations from
adjacent specialties: Pediatric endocrinology must provide the results
of the pending laboratory tests (Table 1) to guide further
cross-sectional imaging decisions.

blocks.en:
An 8-year-old boy presented with an 18-month history of a right breast
mass that enlarged over the preceding 6 months, accompanied by fine
pubic and scant axillary hair but with prepubertal testes (3 mL) and a
prepubertal phallus (DOI: 10.1056/NEJMcpc1503831 ). Breast ultrasound
demonstrated a 1.4 × \times 1.3 × \times 0.8 cm well-circumscribed, oval, hypoechoic,
hypovascular retroareolar mass with through-transmission, smooth
margins, and parallel orientation, lacking malignant features; the left
breast showed a normal bud (DOI: 10.1056/NEJMcpc1503831 , Figure 1). The
leading hypothesis is a juvenile fibroadenoma, given the discrete,
nodular morphology with classic benign solid-lesion features, though
unilateral gynecomastia driven by early adrenarche remains a
consideration. Bone age is concordant with chronological age, arguing
against chronic systemic sex-steroid excess. Priority actions are to
perform scrotal ultrasound to exclude a non-palpable testicular neoplasm
and to review the pending laboratory values (Table 1) to determine if
adrenal imaging is warranted. If targeted imaging and laboratory results
are negative, follow-up breast ultrasound in 3 to 6 months is
appropriate. The most impactful data gaps are the missing laboratory
values (Table 1) and the unreported results of the chest imaging
performed 13 days after presentation, both of which are essential to
narrow the differential and direct further workup.

blocks.en:
An 8-year-old boy presents with an 18-month history of a right
retroareolar breast mass that has enlarged over the last 6 months,
accompanied by the recent onset of fine pubic and axillary hair.
Physical examination reveals a firm, mobile 2x2 cm mass under the right
areola, a small left breast bud, prepubertal testes (3 ml), and a
prepubertal phallus. Bone age is concordant with chronological age (8
years). Breast ultrasound shows a well-circumscribed, oval, hypoechoic,
hypovascular mass with benign features. The specialists agree that the
presentation is most consistent with a benign localized process (either
prepubertal gynecomastia or a fibroepithelial lesion such as a
fibroadenoma) in the setting of premature adrenarche, while central
precocious puberty is excluded. Critical data gaps include the
unprovided results of Table 1 laboratory tests and chest imaging. There
is a disagreement regarding the next diagnostic step: radiology favors
conservative observation with follow-up ultrasound, while surgery and
pathology favor tissue diagnosis via excisional or core needle biopsy
due to the mass's persistence, size, and enlargement.

blocks.en: Purpose of the assessment

blocks.en:
The purpose of the assessment is to evaluate the quality of an already
generated medical consensus report, rather than to reassess the patient or the
source article. The physician rater should assign numeric scores in the
spreadsheet and, when needed, provide a concise explanation of the main
deficiencies.

而不是重新评估患者或

电子表格,并在需要时,简要地解释
缺点。

blocks.en:
• Evaluate only what is explicitly stated in the consensus report and
supported by the source clinical case. • Do not infer missing information on behalf of the report author. If a
relevant fact, test result, diagnosis, or explanation is absent, treat it as
absent. • Do not assign a high score solely because the text is fluent or
well-structured if it contains fabricated data, weak clinical logic, or an
unsafe management strategy. • All numeric scores in the spreadsheet must be 0, 1, 2, or 3.

Each case contains three evaluated report components. The same eight criteria

transferred automatically to another component: a strong final conclusion does
not compensate for weak reasoning, and strong reasoning does not compensate for
an inadequate final conclusion.

Rule for fabricated facts
blocks.zh: 关于捏造事实的规则

blocks.en:
A fabricated fact is a clinically significant test result, numerical value,
date, symptom, diagnosis, complication, procedure, or treatment that is absent
from the source case but is presented by the consensus report as an established
fact.
blocks.zh:
捏造的事实是临床上重要的测试结果 数值
缺席的日期、症状、诊断、并发症、程序或治疗
,但以协商一致报告的形式作为确定
事实上

blocks.en:
• If a fabricated fact affects the diagnosis, differential diagnosis,
final conclusion, or management strategy, the criterion “Factual accuracy
and sources” should receive 0 points. • If the reasoning, differential diagnosis, final conclusion, or
management strategy is based on the fabricated fact, the corresponding
criteria should receive no more than 1 point. • If the fabricated fact creates a risk of unsafe treatment or omission
of an important threat, the criterion “Clinical safety” should also receive
no more than 1 point. • The comment should specify which fact was fabricated and how it was
used in the report.

blocks.en: Procedure for scoring one case row
blocks.zh: 评分一行案件的程序

blocks.en:
1. Identify the case number in the spreadsheet. 2. Read the clinical case description, including the patient
characteristics, main complaints, important laboratory results, imaging,
clinical course, treatment, and safety risks. 3. In the pre-consensus stage, identify the block corresponding to the
rater’s specialty. 4. Assign eight scores for the “Reasoning” component in columns B–I. 5. In the same specialty-specific block, identify the “Final conclusion”
section and assign eight scores for the “First-stage final judgment”
component in columns J–Q. 6. Proceed to the overall consensus stage and assign eight scores for the
“Consensus conclusion” component in columns R–Y. 7. Assign the whole-case scores: column Z for adequacy of the specialist
composition, column AA for clinical complexity, and column AB for the overall
quality of all stages. The complexity score is the rater’s expert judgment
from the perspective of the rater’s specialty. 8. Complete the general comment in column AC. Scores of 0 or 1 should be
explained whenever possible.

blocks.en: Criterion-specific scoring rules
blocks.zh: 特定标准评分规则

blocks.en: Factual accuracy and sources
blocks.zh: 事实准确性和来源

blocks.en:
Assess whether the facts in the consensus report match the source case,
including symptoms, dates, laboratory values, test results, diagnoses,
procedures, and treatments.
blocks.zh:
评估协商一致报告中的事实是否与来文方的案件相符,
包括症状、日期、实验室值、测试结果、诊断、
程序和治疗。

blocks.en: Identification and prioritization of clinical problems
blocks.zh: 临床问题的确定和优先排序

blocks.en:
Assess whether the report identifies what is clinically central, what is
secondary, and what represents an immediate threat.
blocks.zh:
评估报告是否确定了临床上的核心内容,什么是
次要的,什么是直接的威胁。

blocks.en: Completeness and relevance of the data used
blocks.zh: 所用数据的完整性和相关性

blocks.en:
Assess whether the report uses the data required to make a reliable diagnosis
or select an appropriate management strategy.
blocks.zh:
评估报告是否使用可靠诊断所需的数据
或选择适当的管理战略。

blocks.en: Coherence of clinical reasoning
blocks.zh: 临床推理的一致性

blocks.en:
Assess whether the report contains a valid causal and inferential chain rather
than a set of disconnected statements.
blocks.zh:
评估报告是否包含一个有效的因果关系和推断链,而不是
而不是一组断开的语句。

blocks.en: Quality of differential diagnosis
blocks.zh: 差异诊断的质量

blocks.en:
Assess whether plausible alternatives are considered rather than a single
preferred diagnosis.
blocks.zh:
评估是否考虑可行的替代品而不是单一的替代品
更喜欢的诊断。

blocks.en: Quality of the final clinical conclusion
blocks.zh: 最后临床结论的质量

blocks.en:
Assess whether the final conclusion answers the main clinical question: what is
most likely occurring, how well this is supported, and what remains uncertain.
blocks.zh:
评估最后结论是否回答了主要的临床问题:
最有可能发生的情况,对此的支持程度如何,哪些因素仍然不确定。

blocks.en: Justification and specificity of management strategy
blocks.zh: 管理战略的理由和具体性

blocks.en:
Assess whether the plan can be acted upon clinically: what should be done,
when, why, and what the next step should be.
blocks.zh:
评估是否可以在临床上采取行动:应做些什么,
什么时候,为什么,以及下一步应该是什么。

blocks.en: Clinical safety
blocks.zh: 临床安全

blocks.en:
Assess whether the consensus report creates risk for the patient or omits
threats that require immediate monitoring or action.
blocks.zh:
评估协商一致报告是否给患者带来风险或遗漏
需要立即监测或采取行动的威胁。

blocks.en: Whole-case criteria
blocks.zh: 全案标准

blocks.en:
These three scores are assigned once per case row and are not repeated for each
component. The rater should evaluate the consensus report as a whole.
blocks.zh:
这三个分数是每个案件一行一次的,每个不重复
组件。 评定员应对整个协商一致报告进行评价。

blocks.en: Adequacy of specialist composition, column Z
blocks.zh: 专家构成的充分性,Z栏

blocks.en:
Assess whether the selected specialists were clinically necessary for resolving
the case.
blocks.zh:
评估选定专家在临床上是否对解决
那个案子

blocks.en: Clinical complexity of the case, column AA
blocks.zh: 案件临床复杂程度,AA栏

blocks.en:
This score reflects the difficulty of the case itself, not the quality of the
generated consensus report. A poorly written consensus report does not make the
case more complex. The score represents the rater’s specialty-specific expert
judgment: 0 indicates a case that is simple for the rater’s specialty and for
which the need for a consensus is questionable; 3 indicates a very complex case
for which convening a consensus is highly appropriate.
blocks.zh:
这个分数反映了案件本身的困难,而不是质量
形成了共识报告。 书面的协商一致报告并不能使
比较复杂 评分代表评分专家的特长
判决: 0 表示一个对评估者专业和
3 表明一个非常复杂的情况
就此达成共识是非常适当的。

blocks.en: Overall quality of all consensus stages, column AB
blocks.zh: 所有协商一致阶段的总体质量,AB栏

blocks.en:
This is a global expert judgment of whether the consensus report is usable as a
coherent clinical product.
blocks.zh:
这是全球专家对协商一致报告是否可作为
一致的临床产品。

blocks.en: Writing comments
blocks.zh: 写入注释

blocks.en:
The comment should not restate the entire case. Its purpose is to make clear
why low scores were assigned and where the main deficiency is located.
blocks.zh:
评论不应重复整个案例。 其目的是要明确
为何分配的分数低,主要缺陷所在。

blocks.en:
• A comment should be provided when any score of 0 or 1 is assigned. • For fabricated facts, specify the exact fact and explain why it is not
present in the source data. • If the assessment is generally favorable, one concise sentence about
the main limitation is sufficient. If there are no major problems, the field
may be left blank. • Avoid non-specific comments such as “many errors,” “acceptable but
could be better,” or “poor conclusion” unless the problem is specified.
